subject: maths
title: Indices, Surds and Logarithms
welcome_lead: Sharpen your algebra: master indices, surd manipulation and the laws of logarithms.
meta_desc: Maths adventure on indices, surds and logarithm laws with worked examples and practice.
final_note: Logs are inverses of exponentials, never forget the base!

concepts.def: Combinations of numbers, letters and operations.
Writing an expression as a product of factors.
Rules for powers, e.g. xᵃ × xᵇ = xᵃ⁺ᵇ.
Replacing letters with numbers to evaluate.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Solve log_2(x) + log_2(x-2) = 3.

Combine: log_2(x(x-2)) = 3, so x(x-2) = 8. Then x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0, giving x = 4 (reject x = -2).

mcqs.q: If two variables are strongly correlated, what can you conclude?
options: Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
Strong correlation means that one variable causes the other.
(3x + 3)(2x + 3), by trying to factorise as a quadratic.
They vary together — but correlation alone does not establish that one causes the other.

mcqs.q: In the equation y = 3x + 5, what does the 5 represent on the graph?
options: The x value where the line crosses the x-axis.
The gradient — how steep the line is.
Strong correlation means the variables are equal in value.
The y-intercept — the value of y when x = 0 (where the line crosses the y-axis).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Surd”?
options: log_a(x) = log_b(x) / log_b(a).
a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
An irrational root, e.g. √2, kept in exact form.
log_a(x/y) = log_a(x) - log_a(y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Logarithm”?
options: log_a(x/y) = log_a(x) - log_a(y).
log_a(x) = y means a^y = x.
a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
log_a(xy) = log_a(x) + log_a(y).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Change of base”?
options: An irrational root, e.g. √2, kept in exact form.
log_a(xy) = log_a(x) + log_a(y).
a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
log_a(x) = log_b(x) / log_b(a).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Index law”?
options: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
log_a(x/y) = log_a(x) - log_a(y).
log_a(xy) = log_a(x) + log_a(y).
log_a(x) = log_b(x) / log_b(a).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Quotient law”?
options: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
An irrational root, e.g. √2, kept in exact form.
log_a(x/y) = log_a(x) - log_a(y).
log_a(x) = log_b(x) / log_b(a).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Product law”?
options: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n) for the same base a.
log_a(x) = y means a^y = x.
log_a(x) = log_b(x) / log_b(a).
log_a(xy) = log_a(x) + log_a(y).
